90c98fe9b159.title: Certificate Authority
90c98fe9b159.content: An entity that stores, signs, and issues cryptographic certificates and certifies the ownership of a public key by the named subject of the certificate. This allows GDHCN Trust Network Gateway participants to rely on signatures or assertions made in relation to the private key corresponding to the certified public key. Certificate Authorities may be operated by different types of entities, including, but not limited to, a private-sector Certificate Authority, a ministry or agency responsible for ICT/eGovernment services, a Ministry of Health, or another competent authority within the jurisdiction. It is the responsibility of each GDHCN Participant to determine the appropriate arrangement for its Certificate Authority, in accordance with applicable laws and policies within its jurisdiction, to guarantee security and proper data management. Each GDHCN Participant must identify, establish, or liaise with the relevant Certificate Authority, as applicable and impose on the latter all requirements of this document.

597497c4693e.title: GDHCN Trust Network
597497c4693e.content: The GDHCN Trust Network is a Trust Network comprised of the GDHCN Secretariat and GDHCN Participants. The GDHCN Trust Network operationalizes Trust Domains through a Trust Network Gateway by enabling bilateral verification and utilization of Verifiable Digital Health Certificates and the utilization of Trusted Services by GDHCN Participants.

61a7ccbeb2ac.title: Eligible GDHCN Participant
61a7ccbeb2ac.content: An Eligible GDHCN Participant is one of the following: • a WHO Member State or Associate Member, or sub-national unit thereof; • a State Party to the International Health Regulations (2005), or sub-national unit thereof; • the United Nations (UN) and other intergovernmental organizations in effective relations with WHO; • a fund, programme, specialized agency, or related organization within the UN system; or • an organization officially delegated by one of the organizations mentioned above that can abide by the GDHCN Terms of Participation and fulfils one or more of the following health service functions: • Public Health Agency; • Health Professions Education Accreditation Agency; • Health Services Licensing Agency; or • Public Health Security Agency. and, once accepted to the GDHCN, after the successful conclusion of the Onboarding Process, will be referred to as GDHCN Participant throughout this document. An Eligible GDHCN Participant that has initiated the Onboarding Process will be referred to as an Eligible GDHCN Applicant throughout this document. Quoted from Section II of the Framework. 7b8871aa0895.title: Health Services Licensing Agency
7b8871aa0895.content: An organization or organizational unit that is responsible for establishing and/or implementing procedures for licensure, and the licensing of organizations or individuals to provide clinical, health system or public health services within their jurisdiction. 33d2e9918149.title: Verifiable Digital Health Certificate

Trusted Service A service (digital or otherwise) related to the issuance, management, verification, exchange, or other relevant processes, of Verifiable Digital Health Certificates which is defined using open, interoperable digital health standards. b14fe23d14f9.title: V
b14fe23d14f9.content: Verifiable Digital Health Certificate A digital representation of a data set comprising a certificate or document, designed for a set of specific clinical or public health use cases which is defined using open, interoperable digital health standards; that contains within, or is associated to, a digital signature which can be verified by the public key of a public-private encryption key pair, and which is issued by a GDHCN Participant. df257caa1c31.title: Already somebody else’s concept?
df257caa1c31.content: Extracted candidates are minted from this repository’s own assets and are not, by themselves, checked against any vocabulary. check:term-mapping asks whether each already exists as a concept somebody is authoritative for — SKOS for what a term MEANS, FHIR for a clinical code’s operational semantics — and the two are separate questions with separate answers.
